label: Tiny Engines
description: Truth Club's debut pairs Chris Davis's conversational, self-lacerating lyrics with tense, angular guitar interplay that snaps between quiet verses and squalling choruses. It sounds like a Raleigh house-show band that grew up on Pavement and Cap'n Jazz in equal measure. Good for listeners who want their slacker rock a little more wound-up and anxious.
lineage: Grows out of the Pavement/GBV lineage of loud-quiet indie rock filtered through Raleigh's DIY basement scene; feeds directly into the tighter, more melodic songwriting of Running From the Chase.

label: Double Double Whammy
description: A more confident, widescreen version of the Truth Club sound, moving from hushed confession to full-band catharsis with a voice that cracks at the edges of big, hooky choruses. It plays like a document of getting older and more self-aware without losing any of the tension of the debut.
lineage: Continues Truth Club's basement-scene, Pavement/GBV-descended jangle-and-noise songwriting into a more polished, emotionally direct register.

label: Don Giovanni
description: Katie Crutchfield's bedroom-recorded debut, written and tracked in a week at her family home, is just acoustic guitar and a cracked, plainspoken voice working through devastation and longing. It is the rawest end of the slacker/DIY spectrum this lane covers, closer to a diary than a studio record.
lineage: Grows out of the DIY punk and cassette/Bandcamp network Crutchfield came up in, and sounds indebted to the deadpan funny-sad songwriting line; it seeds her entire catalog, including her later, more country-leaning work covered elsewhere in this atlas.
borderline_note: Pre-2020 Waxahatchee records are placed in C7 (slacker/lo-fi) with C3 as secondary since her songwriting already leans country-folk; the post-2020 Merge albums fit C3/V lanes better and are out of this lane's scope.

label: Don Giovanni
description: Recorded at home with Swearin's Kyle Gilbride, this is a fuller-sounding but still homemade record about family, addiction and young adulthood in Alabama. The song-to-song shift between fragile acoustic pieces and full-band fuzz set the template for a decade of Waxahatchee records.
lineage: Extends American Weekend's DIY lo-fi songwriting with Swearin'-band muscle; a key transitional record between bedroom-pop slacker rock and Crutchfield's later, more countryish songwriting.

label: Merge
description: Waxahatchee's Merge debut loosens the structure further, mixing drum machines and organ drones into the guitar songs for a woozier, more experimental slacker record. It is the least polished-sounding of her Merge albums and the closest to classic 90s indie rock.
lineage: Bridges Cerulean Salt's basement sound with a more expansive, era-blurring indie rock palette; part of the same Merge-era run that established Crutchfield as an indie rock and later Americana songwriter.

label: Merge
description: Produced with John Agnello and her touring band, this is Waxahatchee's loudest, most straightforwardly indie-rock record, about the end of a relationship. It trades the lo-fi hush of her earlier albums for full-band immersion and sharper, angrier hooks.
lineage: The full-band endpoint of Waxahatchee's slacker/DIY period before she moved toward the more countryish Saint Cloud and Tigers Blood.

label: Captured Tracks
description: DeMarco's Captured Tracks debut coined the woozy, chorus-pedal 'jizz jazz' sound that defined blog-era slacker rock: loose, warbly guitar lines, half-mumbled vocals and a stoned, unhurried tempo throughout. It set the template for a decade of goofball-slacker singer-songwriters.
lineage: Sounds indebted to Pavement's shambling guitar pop and Flying Nun-style DIY jangle; its own influence on the 2010s slacker-rock and bedroom-pop wave that followed is well established.

label: Captured Tracks
description: DeMarco's best-known record is a warmer, more melodic take on his slacker sound, about the anxieties of encroaching adulthood delivered with a shrug. The title track and 'Passing Out Pieces' became blog-rock standards.
lineage: Refines the '2' blueprint into DeMarco's signature sound; a touchstone for the 2010s jangle/slacker revival.

label: Captured Tracks
description: A quieter, more acoustic-leaning record built around fingerpicked guitar and synth textures, dealing with DeMarco's relationship with his father. Still slacker in tone but more reflective than his earlier records.
lineage: Shows the slacker-rock lineage bending toward hushed singer-songwriter territory.

label: Mac's Record Label
description: Self-released on DeMarco's own label, this record strips his sound to its most repetitive and hypnotic, with simple, mantra-like song structures and titles. A deliberately low-key follow-up that trades hooks for mood.
lineage: DeMarco's move to self-release on his own label echoes the DIY spirit this lane traces.

label: Sub Pop
description: Three guitarists trading melodic, chiming lines over motorik rhythms, with plainspoken, road-trip lyrics about growing up and moving on. It is one of the cleanest modern distillations of the Flying Nun/Go-Betweens jangle sound.
lineage: Sounds indebted to Antipodean jangle-pop (The Clean, The Go-Betweens); part of the 2010s Australian guitar-pop wave alongside The Goon Sax and Twerps.

label: Sub Pop
description: A sunnier, more confident sequel to Hope Downs, with the same three-guitar interlock but bigger choruses and warmer production. Written partly about touring and homesickness.
lineage: Sounds like second-generation Flying Nun-indebted jangle-pop, continuing the band's refinement of the sound.

label: Sub Pop
description: A darker, more expansive record with longer song structures and heavier guitar tones layered under the band's signature three-guitar jangle. It is the band's most textured album, for listeners who want the chime with more shadow.
lineage: Shows the band stretching its Flying Nun-indebted jangle sound toward denser, more textured arrangements.

label: You've Changed Records
description: Nigel Chapman's conversational, half-spoken vocals ride over loose, unhurried jangle-rock guitar, closer to Jonathan Richman or Silver Jews than most of their slacker-rock peers. Bookish, philosophical lyrics over simple, warm arrangements.
lineage: Sounds indebted to the deadpan funny-sad songwriting line (Silver Jews/Drag City) crossed with VU-style jangle guitar; the start of one of the decade's most consistent guitar-rock runs.

label: Paradise of Bachelors
description: A more assured, road-tested version of the band's talky jangle-rock, with Chapman's lyrics turning toward philosophy and self-doubt over bright, ringing guitar lines. Songs like 'Stargazer' stretch out patiently, for listeners who like their indie rock literate and unhurried.
lineage: Continues the band's jangle songwriting, which sounds indebted to Silver Jews and the Velvet Underground.

label: Jagjaguwar
description: A slightly more polished, full-band record that keeps Nigel Chapman's signature talk-singing but adds more melodic hooks and confident guitar solos. It is the band's most accessible entry point, warm and ringing without losing its bookish, self-questioning lyrics.
lineage: Third album in Nap Eyes' jangle/talk-song lineage, moving toward a bigger label and wider audience.

label: Royal Mountain Records
description: Nap Eyes' most direct, hook-forward record, still built on Chapman's conversational delivery but with brighter, more confident arrangements.
lineage: Continues the band's jangle/talk-song lineage into a fourth album.

label: You've Changed Records
description: The band pairs its conversational, bookish lyrics with sunny organ and strong, ringing guitar work. Nigel Chapman's half-spoken delivery stays at the center, making it a warm late-career entry for fans of talky, unhurried guitar rock.
lineage: Latest chapter in Nap Eyes' jangle songwriting, which sounds indebted to Silver Jews and the Velvet Underground.

label: Earth Libraries
description: A warm, crisp midtempo jangle record built around layered melodies and unvarnished lyricism, with pedal steel coloring several tracks. It stakes out its own lane of graceful, inviting jangle-pop for listeners who like their guitar pop gentle.
lineage: Sounds indebted to the DIY jangle/college-radio line (Big Star, Flying Nun), filtered through 2020s Midwest indie rock.

label: Self-released
description: Cooper's third album trades the jam-guitar sound of her earlier band for a crisper, Beck-like mix of fuzz bass, piano and twinkling synths. It is warm, direct pop-rock songwriting with a slacker's DIY informality, for listeners who like hooks with a homemade edge.
lineage: Sounds like a former jam/psych-rock guitarist moving toward a more concise, jangle-adjacent indie-pop songwriting style.
borderline_note: Cooper's earlier work as Liz Cooper & the Stampede is more jam/psych-rock and sits outside this lane's slacker/jangle/power-pop definition; only New Day is included here.

label: Curation Records
description: A Los Angeles band's debut LP, blending frantic C86-style jangle-pop with post-punk urgency and a touch of Flying Nun. Ten songs of tightly wound guitar interplay and restless energy.
lineage: A direct 2020s continuation of the Flying Nun/C86 jangle lineage that runs through this whole lane.

label: Born Yesterday Records
description: A New Orleans duo splitting the difference between breezy power-pop hooks and nervy post-punk edges, with trading vocals and taut, bright guitars. It sits in the same power-pop revival as Dazy, 2nd Grade and Mo Troper.
lineage: Sounds indebted to the Big Star power-pop line crossed with post-punk tension, part of the mid-2020s power-pop revival.

label: Exploding In Sound Records
description: Lawn's most confident record yet, a scrappy blend of post-punk and power-pop with dual lead vocals trading off across hook-heavy songs. It is a punchy distillation of the New Orleans band's sound, wiry guitars and all.
lineage: Continues Lawn's power-pop/post-punk hybrid songwriting into a bigger, punchier register.

label: Matador
description: Lindsey Jordan's teenage debut pairs plainspoken, diaristic lyrics with clean, jangly guitar leads that build into big, cathartic choruses. A defining record of the 2010s slacker-rock revival's younger generation.
lineage: Sounds indebted to 90s and 2000s guitar songwriters like Liz Phair and Rilo Kiley and to the Bandcamp-era DIY scene; it became a touchstone for the wave of young guitar-pop songwriters that followed.

label: Matador
description: A more produced, emotionally raw follow-up to Lush, adding synths and string arrangements to Jordan's core jangle-guitar sound. Her voice pushes into more theatrical territory, for listeners who want the heartbreak bigger and glossier.
lineage: Second chapter of Snail Mail's slacker-to-art-pop evolution.

label: Fat Possum Records
description: Sophie Allison's breakout record moves her Bandcamp bedroom-pop into full-band arrangements. It is still built on quiet, confessional verses and 90s-alt-rock-indebted guitar hooks about jealousy and self-doubt.
lineage: Grows out of the Bandcamp/DIY bedroom-pop network and 90s alt-rock guitar songwriting; a borderline case whose pop instincts push toward Context-lane crossover on later records.
borderline_note: Soccer Mommy sits close to the Context pop-crossover boundary; Clean is included here for its DIY/slacker guitar-pop sound, but her more polished later albums (color theory onward) lean further toward mainstream alt-pop.

label: Woodsist
description: A hazy, reverb-soaked debut about suburban New Jersey boredom, built on interlocking clean-toned guitar lines and unhurried tempos. A foundational record for the 2010s jangle revival.
lineage: Sounds indebted to Flying Nun/Feelies-style jangle guitar pop; a key node connecting classic jangle to the 2010s slacker/jangle scene.

label: Domino
description: A cleaner, more melodic refinement of the band's suburban jangle-pop sound. Warm, mid-tempo guitar interplay sits under gentle, nostalgic lyrics, for listeners who like their indie rock hazy and summery.
lineage: Continues Real Estate's jangle catalog, which sounds indebted to Flying Nun and the Feelies.
borderline_note: Real Estate's post-2011 albums (Atlas onward) move toward a mellower, more adult-alternative sound better suited to a Context lane; only the early, DIY-jangle-scene records are placed here.

label: Carpark
description: Sadie Dupuis's knotty, GBV/Pavement-indebted guitar riffs collide with tossed-off, sardonic lyrics across a record that swings between melody and noise. A key 2010s document of the slacker-noise-rock crossover.
lineage: Sounds indebted to Guided by Voices/Pavement's loud-quiet guitar-pop songwriting.

label: Carpark
description: A more confident, bigger-sounding follow-up, with Dupuis's guitar leads pushed further forward and her lyrics turning more pointed and political. Still rooted in the band's angular, GBV-descended riffing.
lineage: Continuation of Speedy Ortiz's Pavement/GBV-indebted noise-pop songwriting.

label: Salinas Records
description: Allison Crutchfield and Kyle Gilbride's band debuts with scrappy, fuzzed-out guitar-pop that splits the difference between 90s indie rock and Philly basement-punk. Direct, unpolished and hook-driven.
lineage: Grows out of the same Philadelphia DIY scene as Waxahatchee and Radiator Hospital, with a guitar-pop sound that seems indebted to Pavement and GBV.

label: Salinas Records
description: A noisier, more layered second record, with dual songwriters Allison Crutchfield and Kyle Gilbride trading lead vocals. Dense, fuzzed guitar interplay drives short, urgent songs built for basement shows.
lineage: Continues Swearin's Philadelphia DIY guitar-pop songwriting, which sounds indebted to Pavement and GBV.

label: Salinas Records
description: Sam Cook-Parrott's project delivers scrappy, hissy, hook-filled songs with a plainspoken, earnest voice at the center. It is unpretentious DIY power-pop-punk in the classic Philly basement mold.
lineage: Part of the same Philadelphia DIY network as Swearin' and Waxahatchee, with a lo-fi guitar-pop sound that recalls Guided by Voices.

label: Salinas Records
description: A denser, more collaborative record built on Cook-Parrott's plainspoken, hook-first songwriting. Short, bright pop-punk songs about love and small humiliations fly by, for fans of basement-show intimacy.
lineage: Continues Radiator Hospital's lo-fi pop-punk songwriting within the Philadelphia DIY scene, with a sound that recalls Guided by Voices.

label: Father Daughter Records
description: A murky, distorted slacker-punk record from a San Francisco band steeped in 90s indie rock, mixing hooky riffs with intentionally lo-fi, gnarled production.
lineage: Descends from Pavement/GBV-style shambling guitar-pop crossed with West Coast noise-punk.

label: Bar/None Records
description: A tighter, more melodic version of Pardoner's slacker-punk sound, still caked in fuzz but with clearer hooks poking through the murk. Fast, messy guitars and yelped vocals make it for listeners who like their indie rock loud and a little unhinged.
lineage: Continuation of Pardoner's Pavement/GBV-descended noisy slacker-pop songwriting.

label: Play Pinball!
description: Parquet Courts' scrappy, self-released debut, full of talky, deadpan vocals and loose, Pavement-indebted guitar interplay recorded on the cheap.
lineage: A direct extension of Pavement's slacker guitar-pop songwriting into a Brooklyn DIY setting.
borderline_note: Early Parquet Courts is placed in C7 for its Pavement-descended slacker sound; from Human Performance onward the band shifts closer to post-punk/noise rock (X10).

label: What's Your Rupture?
description: The breakout record: rambling, funny, deadpan talk-singing over tight guitar interplay that recalls Pavement and the Modern Lovers. It is half stream-of-consciousness and half punk energy, with songs like 'Stoned and Starving' stretching into wiry jams.
lineage: Sounds like the clearest 2010s inheritor of Pavement's slacker guitar-pop songwriting.
borderline_note: Included as C7's clearest Pavement-descended slacker record from this band; later albums move toward post-punk (X10).

label: Chapter Music
description: A hazy, unhurried debut of ramshackle jangle-pop from Melbourne, indebted to the Flying Nun and Feelies sound. The vocals are offhand and half-mumbled, for listeners who like their guitar pop loose and sunlit.
lineage: Sounds indebted to Flying Nun jangle-pop and the Go-Betweens/Clean lineage; part of the same 2010s Australian guitar-pop wave as Rolling Blackouts Coastal Fever and The Goon Sax.

label: Chapter Music
description: A more polished, dreamier follow-up, with brighter production but the same loose jangle songwriting at its core. Male and female vocals trade off over chiming guitars, keeping the debut's casual charm.
lineage: Continues Twerps' jangle-pop, which sounds indebted to Flying Nun and the Go-Betweens.

label: Upset The Rhythm
description: A Melbourne group with members of Total Control and UV Race debuts with wiry, deadpan guitar-pop songs about everyday minutiae. It sounds closer to a shaggier Flying Nun update than to noise rock, for fans of dry humor and trebly guitars.
lineage: Grows out of Melbourne's DIY jangle/post-punk scene and sounds related to the same Australian guitar-pop wave as Rolling Blackouts Coastal Fever and Twerps.

label: Self-released
description: Released while the band was still called Sports, this self-released debut is scrappy, hooky basement pop-punk. Fast, fuzzy guitars and wry, confessional lyrics set up everything the band would polish later.
lineage: Sounds indebted to GBV/Pavement guitar-pop songwriting by way of the East Coast DIY scene.

label: Father/Daughter
description: A tighter, more anthemic record than the band's early lo-fi releases, mixing power-pop hooks with the same wry, self-aware lyrics. Carmen Perry's bright, direct voice leads punchy, fuzzed guitars built for singing along.
lineage: Continues the Philadelphia DIY-to-power-pop path, sounding of a piece with the later power-pop revival of Lawn and Sharp Pins.

label: Get Better Records
description: An anthemic yet intimate pop-rock record that sits between energetic and vulnerable songwriting. It continues the band's move from scrappy Philadelphia basement pop-punk toward bigger power-pop hooks.
lineage: Latest chapter of Remember Sports' Philadelphia DIY power-pop lineage.

label: Manic Static
description: A kinetic Chicago DIY debut mixing jangly, interlocking guitar lines with garage-rock urgency. It is the first half of a strong two-album run, for listeners who like their jangle fast and loud.
lineage: Sounds indebted to Flying Nun/Feelies jangle crossed with garage-rock energy, rooted in Chicago's DIY venue scene.

label: Grand Jury Music
description: The second half of NE-HI's two-album run, with sharper songwriting and more melodic hooks. The same jangly, fuzz-toned guitar interplay drives it, now with cleaner production and more room to breathe.
lineage: Continuation of NE-HI's jangle/garage-rock songwriting within Chicago's DIY scene.

label: Self-released
description: A cohesive, jittery-warm record of jangle-pop songwriting from a Grand Rapids band. It mixes heavy rock'n'roll textures with pop hooks, built to be heard as a full album.
lineage: Sounds indebted to Big Star/Flying Nun jangle-pop songwriting by way of the Midwest DIY circuit.

label: Lame-O Records
description: Fifteen hook-dense power-pop tracks from a Portland songwriter, pairing clever, self-aware writing with warmth and classic melodies. Troper's own tagline calls his style 'the Conker's Bad Fur Day of power pop,' which captures its mix of nerdy reference and sugar rush.
lineage: Direct descendant of the Big Star/Teenage Fanclub power-pop lineage, part of the 2020s power-pop revival alongside Sharp Pins and Lawn.

label: Hallogallo Tapes
description: Kai Slater's (Lifeguard, Dwaal Troupe) solo power-pop project delivers bedroom-recorded, Big Star/Teenage Fanclub-style hooks. Short, jangly songs come wrapped in scrappy tape-hiss charm, for listeners who like their power pop homemade.
lineage: Sounds indebted to the Big Star power-pop lineage by way of lo-fi, self-recorded bedroom pop.

album: Box for Buddy, Box for Star
label: Double Double Whammy
description: Nate Amos's (Water From Your Eyes) solo project delivers warped, hooky pop songs that recall the Postal Service, Big Star and the Magnetic Fields. Drum machines and home-recorded synths sit under genuine power-pop songwriting, sweet and slightly off-kilter.
lineage: Sounds indebted to Big Star power-pop songwriting, filtered through home-recorded, synth-augmented indie pop.
key_tracks: Box for Buddy, Box for Star

label: Autumn Tone
description: Twin Peaks' scrappy debut is all ragged garage-jangle riffs and teenage swagger. Short, shouted songs and loose, bashing drums capture a young Chicago band playing fast and not overthinking it.
lineage: Rooted in Chicago's teenage DIY scene, with a sound that recalls garage rock and Pavement-style slacker guitar-pop.

label: Grand Jury Music
description: A tighter, more craft-oriented second LP that mixes ragged jangle-pop with rowdy garage energy. Multiple singer-songwriters trade short, catchy songs, making it the band's most instantly fun record.
lineage: Continuation of Twin Peaks' garage-jangle songwriting, moving toward wider recognition.

label: Self-released
description: A big step up for the band, with keyboards and horns thickening the rowdy garage-jangle sound and the songwriting reaching for Stones- and Faces-style classic-rock scope. It is looser and warmer than Wild Onion, for listeners who like their bar-band rock young and ragged.
lineage: Builds on Wild Onion's Chicago garage-jangle sound while sounding newly indebted to '70s classic rock.
key_tracks: Walk to the One You Love

label: Self-released
description: A warmer, more classic-rock-leaning record that rounds out the band's transition from scrappy garage kids to accomplished songwriters. Piano, harmonies and relaxed grooves replace much of the old rowdiness, for fans of easygoing '70s-style rock.
lineage: Later-period Twin Peaks, still rooted in the band's Chicago garage-jangle scene origins.

label: Self-released
description: An early record mixing jangly guitar with drum machines and synths in an off-kilter, homemade pop style. It feels like a bedroom experiment in progress, for listeners who enjoy lo-fi indie rock that wanders.
lineage: Part of the DIY/Bandcamp jangle-pop network this lane traces from Flying Nun and college radio.

label: Self-released
description: A knotty, chameleonic indie rock record mixing jangle, synths and drum machines. At least one song sounds like a lost Pavement track, making it a rewarding listen for fans of homemade, shape-shifting guitar pop.
lineage: Continues Zook's homemade jangle/synth-pop hybrid songwriting, which sounds indebted to Pavement's slacker guitar-pop.

label: Winspear
description: Indiana songwriters Kevin Krauter and Nina Pitchkites blend shoegaze haze, grunge fuzz and power-pop hooks on their debut LP. It moves between pillowy atmospherics and scathing distortion, for fans of melodic, loud '90s-style guitar rock.
lineage: Sounds indebted to the Big Star power-pop line crossed with 90s alt-rock guitar tones.

label: Winspear
description: A New Orleans duo's fourth LP moves away from disco nostalgia toward more personal, unselfconscious songwriting. Its effortless-sounding hooks and smooth pop craft recall Steely Dan and the Beach Boys.
lineage: Descends from breezy 70s pop-rock songwriting filtered through 2010s New Orleans indie pop.

label: Electric Muse
description: A Busan band's debut full-length, applying warm, ringing jangle-pop guitar tones to plainspoken, sea-town songwriting. It is the start of a consistently pristine throwback indie-rock run, understated and melodic.
lineage: Sounds indebted to Flying Nun/Byrds-style jangle-pop, transplanted to the Korean indie scene.

label: Damnably
description: Sun-bleached, reverb-drenched jangle-pop that recalls the Byrds by way of Real Estate. Sumi Choi's calm, plainspoken vocals float over chiming and occasionally surging guitars, for listeners who like their indie rock pristine and wistful.
lineage: Continues Say Sue Me's jangle-pop songwriting, which sounds indebted to Flying Nun and the Byrds.

label: Trouble in Mind
description: A Welsh band's debut applies ringing, Byrds/Feelies-style jangle guitar to raw, personal songwriting about grief and family, one of the sharpest post-2020s jangle-revival records.
lineage: Direct descendant of classic jangle-pop (The Feelies, early R.E.M., Flying Nun bands).

label: Trouble in Mind
description: A follow-up that keeps The Tubs' chiming jangle-pop core while broadening the arrangements. It continues the band's run of sharply written, classic-sounding guitar-pop, with bright leads and a dry, baritone lead voice.
lineage: Continues The Tubs' jangle-pop, which sounds indebted to '80s British and Antipodean guitar pop.
